label: miso27b interchange shape full
definition: (PROBE) miso25 flag set + full --interchange-shaping (both legs, default percentile=90): shape the priced interchange node by the measured EIA-930 (month x hour-of-day) net-interchange envelope — import availability capped overnight-deep/midday-shallow, export min_gen released to the measured midday export. FIXES gap (1), the diurnal volatility: peak->trough swing drops to 1959/1636/1674 MW (2023/24/25) from miso25's ~4832, vs actual 1020/999/1471 — the measured deliverability envelope (admissible rule #12, same class as miso_seam_flow_limit) is the right structure and stays. BUT overcorrects the LEVEL: net imports now UNDERSHOOT actual — 23.93/13.79/10.28 TWh vs actual 37.9/23.1/19.0 (miso25 overshot 46.7/32.4/21.4). Root cause is structural and documented in inject_interchange_shape: the full shape caps *gross* import availability at the *net*-import envelope (net << gross since MISO imports AND exports across different seams), starving baseload imports — the LP imports ~100% of hours (2023/24) but the per-hour cap binds low. Import depth too shallow at every percentile (2023 p10/p50/p90 -4502/-2714/-538 vs actual -7130/-4330/-1596). Collateral: 2025 coal over-runs (+26 TWh vs EIA-923) backfilling the missing imports; energy-balance drift -4.5/-4.8 TWh in 2024/25. Lever for the level is the code's designed INTERCHANGE_SHAPE_IMPORT_PCT 'bidir sweep' (fatten the deliverable overnight tail) -> miso27c (import_pct=97). NO firm floor, energy_reserve_coopt OFF.
